title: ArchitecturalBuildingBlock
description:
A reusable technical component named by its ROLE, decoupled from any concrete implementation. Zurich's E-RDA2 uses the same abstraction — ABB.03 = DATABASE has slots that DB2, ADLS, BLOB, XYZ or CaaS can fill — because it lets a vendor swap be a one-manifest edit rather than a call-site rewrite. Without an ABB layer, a service is inseparable from its implementation and 'we use Postgres' becomes a load-bearing invariant across the codebase.

The estate has ~74 services today and no ABB abstraction between them and the capability map — this schema adds it. A MeshActionRegistry participant declares `implementsAbb: ['ABB.03']` and immediately becomes a swappable slot filler. `capabilityShape(abbId)` (in libs/python) then returns every service claiming the role, ranked by trust score.

This is a spec, not an implementation choice. What makes an ABB an ABB is that it CANNOT be authored beside the code that consumes it — a hand-maintained shape list drifts the moment someone adds a service. Consumers derive the set by walking MeshActionRegistry, filtering on `implementsAbb`, verifying signatures. Same discipline as the intent-grid: derive from the canon, never author alongside it.

abbId.description: Two-digit ABB identifier (ABB.01, ABB.02, ..., ABB.99). Namespaced by role, not by vendor — vendor is a property of the implementation, not the block. ABBs are numbered stably: renumbering an ABB is a breaking change to every manifest that references it, so ids are assigned once and never reused.

role.description:
Canonical role, from a CLOSED set. The same names Zurich uses, deliberately, because they name FUNCTIONS not TECHNOLOGIES: 'PostgreSQL' is not a role, 'DATABASE' is.

Why an enum and not a validated string: this field was `{type: string, minLength: 1}` and the vendor denial lived in a code-side deny list that was never applied to a document (see tools/validate_architectural_building_block.py). A deny list also cannot prevent the OTHER failure, which is the one that actually compounds — the same role spelled several ways. macOS ships 627 sandbox containers whose extension-point names include `extension` (45×), `Extension` (2×), `DiagnosticExtension` (8×), `diagnosticextension` (5×) and `diagnostic` (3×): fifteen years of a freeform role field with no enforced grammar, after which the name can no longer be used to group anything and a side-channel record has to carry the contract instead. An allowlist forecloses both failures at once, and forecloses them in the SCHEMA, which is applied to every document — unlike a validator's private regex.

The set is closed on purpose and is grounded in roles actually in use (prophet-mesh specs/abb-catalog.yaml plus the shipped example), never on roles we imagine wanting. Adding a role is therefore a spec PR: a reviewed edit here, which is exactly the gatekeeping step whose absence produced the five spellings above. If you need a role that is not listed, add it in the same change that adds the ABB document which fills it — a role with no filler is a declared-unenforced field by construction.

description.description: Prose explaining what the role IS and, critically, what it is NOT. Empties are signal: a role with no candidates in the registry is a gap the estate has not filled, not an oversight.

protocol.description: The verbs an implementation of this ABB must be able to answer. Names use the KKO verb ontology so a caller can walk from a capability requirement to an ABB slot without translation.

reads.description: Read-side verbs. Empty is meaningful: a write-only ABB (an event sink) has zero reads by design.

writes.description: Write-side verbs. Same: a read-only ABB (a query surface) has zero writes.

requiredCapabilities.description: Non-functional properties any implementation must satisfy. Machine-checkable in the caller: 'at-rest-encryption', 'row-level-auth', 'audit-chain-append'. A service that fills the slot without carrying every required capability is not a valid filler — the shape derivation rejects it.

conformanceTest.description:
Optional pointer to a conformance test suite (like sourceos-spec/conformance/lawful-verdict-vectors.json for LawfulDispatchReceipt). Two implementations of the same ABB that each pass their own unit tests can still disagree with each other on the ABB's contract — only shared vectors detect that. Present ⇒ implementations are held to it; absent ⇒ conformance is per-implementation and drift is discoverable only by breaking behaviour.

`format: uri-reference` is a SYNTAX check and resolves nothing — this field shipped pointing at `conformance/abb-database-vectors.json`, a file that does not exist, and validated clean. Repo-relative pointers are therefore resolved by tools/validate_pointers_resolve.py, which fails on a dangling one. A pointer to a suite that is not there is worse than absence: absence is documented above as meaningful, whereas a dangling pointer reads as 'held to shared vectors' to every consumer that does not go looking.

supersedes.description: ABB ids this one replaces. Ids are stable, so the old one is not renumbered — it is retired here with a forwarding pointer. A registry walker seeing an old id in a manifest can consult this to warn.
